description: The Shortcodes Ultimate plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Local File Inclusion in versions up to, and including, 7.9.1 This is due to su_get_current_url() interpolating the raw Host request header into the authority portion of a URL that is then passed to esc_url() — which by design preserves '[' and ']' inside the authority so IPv6 literal hosts remain valid — and the [su_qrcode] shortcode substituting that value into its data attribute (the documented %CURRENT_URL% token) before feeding it to do_shortcode(). This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to include arbitrary PHP files that reside within the active theme's root directory (bounded because '/' inside an attribute value terminates parse_url()'s host and is then percent-encoded and stripped), and — when the shipped-default 'Unsafe features' option remains on — to read arbitrary post meta of any post, on any front-end page that renders [su_qrcode data="%CURRENT_URL%"].

The Unbounce Landing Pages plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting in versions up to, and including, 1.1.6. This is due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping on the proxy error message that is persisted to the 'ub-proxy-error-message' option: unauthenticated attacker-controlled REQUEST_URI data is concatenated into the error string in UBHTTP::stream_request_curl()/stream_request_wp_remote() and stored via update_option(), then later echoed inside a <textarea> on the Unbounce Pages Diagnostics admin page without any escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user (an administrator viewing the Diagnostics screen) accesses an injected page.

The One to one user Chat by WPGuppy plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to generic SQL Injection via the 'userId' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.1.6 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. The plugin's permission callback is trivially bypassed because it validates a JWT that the plugin itself signs using an attacker-supplied value from the guppy_guest_account cookie, and the guest code path (userType=0) skips the get_userdata() check that would confirm the userId corresponds to a real WordPress user.
products: amentotechpvtltd / One to one user Chat by WPGuppy

The Restrictions for BuddyPress plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Remote Code Execution in all versions up to, and including, 1.5.4 This is due to the plugin splicing the attacker-controlled request URI into a PHP expression inside a double-quoted string and evaluating it with eval(). The affected conditions ship enabled by default and are evaluated before any logged-in check, so no plugin configuration is needed; the site must have BuddyPress and Paid Memberships Pro active alongside this plugin.

description:

The key is converted with to_string/1 only later, in Phoenix.Presence.group/1, which raises Protocol.UndefinedError on a map. group/1 runs whenever presences are listed and when each presence diff is broadcast, together with the application's fetch/2, which can likewise raise on an unexpected key. Once such a key is tracked, every process that lists presences on the topic crashes, typically each channel that joins it, and presence diffs for the topic are lost.

From 1.7.0 the diff runs in a Task.Supervisor.async task linked to the tracker shard, and Phoenix.Presence.handle_info/2 has no clause for its failure. The shard then terminates, taking down every channel and LiveView process tracked on it and erasing presence state for all its topics. Repeated joins exhaust the restart intensity and take down the application supervisor.

This issue affects phoenix: from 1.2.0 before 1.5.16, from 1.6.0-rc.0 before 1.6.18, from 1.7.0-rc.0 before 1.7.25, and from 1.8.0-rc.0 before 1.8.17.

description:
Uncaught Exception vulnerability in phoenixframework phoenix allows an unauthenticated attacker to cause a denial of service via a client-selected legacy serializer on binary channel broadcasts.

When an application broadcasts {:binary, data} payloads on a channel topic, any client that connects without a vsn parameter, or with vsn=1.0.0, and joins that topic makes those broadcasts fail. Phoenix.Channel.Server.send/4 encodes each broadcast with every subscriber's own serializer inside the PubSub dispatch loop, calling fastlane!/1 with no rescue, and the negotiated Phoenix.Socket.V1.JSONSerializer raises Protocol.UndefinedError on a binary payload. Every binary broadcast on the topic then crashes the broadcasting process and skips every subscriber dispatched after the attacker. For broadcasts arriving from other nodes the loop runs in the PubSub adapter worker, whose repeated crashes restart the PubSub supervisor and empty the node's subscription registry while sockets stay connected.

This issue affects phoenix: from 1.5.7 before 1.5.16, from 1.6.0-rc.0 before 1.6.18, from 1.7.0-rc.0 before 1.7.25, and from 1.8.0-rc.0 before 1.8.17.

@fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.0 through 4.0.9, the plugin joins a path-scoped middleware's mount path to the Fastify plugin prefix by string concatenation, so when the plugin prefix ends with a slash or the mount path omits its leading slash, the resulting Express mount path does not line up with the route the Fastify router serves. Express then fails to match and passes the request on while the Fastify router still dispatches the route, so the middleware is silently skipped. An application that uses path-scoped Express middleware for authentication or authorization inside a prefixed plugin can expose protected routes to unauthenticated clients, with no crafted request and no non-default option required, and string, array, and regular-expression mount paths are all affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

The EoE fragment reassembly code uses a frame size from the wire as the bound for memcpy into the application receive buffer, without checking that the declared size fits in the actual buffer. A master can write up to 2016 bytes into a buffer the application may have sized much smaller.

When the last EoE fragment has the TIME_APPEND flag set, the handler subtracts 4 from rxframeoffset to strip the timestamp. There is no check that rxframeoffset is at least 4. A fragment carrying fewer than 4 bytes of payload that is also marked LAST causes rxframeoffset to wrap to 0xFFFFFFFC, which is then stored as the buffer length and handed to the TCP/IP stack.

The CoE SDO download handler for flexible-length objects (VISIBLE_STRING, OCTET_STRING, and similar) does not check that the master-declared transfer size fits within the object before writing. Two distinct writes are affected: the VISIBLE_STRING zero-padding memset and the first-frame copy into the object buffer.

SDO_downloadsegment is called whenever a mailbox frame carries the DOWNLOADSEGREQ command byte, regardless of whether a segmented download is actually in progress. ESCvar.data, which the handler writes through, is NULL until a segmented transfer is started. A master can send a DOWNLOADSEGREQ at any time and write through a NULL or stale pointer.

The CoE SDO segmented download handler advances a write pointer by each incoming segment's size but does not track how many bytes have been written in total. A master can keep sending non-last segments until the pointer has walked past the end of the object buffer or the complete-access staging buffer.

A CoE SDO request for index 0xFFFF matches the object list terminator entry instead of returning not-found. The terminator has a NULL objdesc pointer. Callers dereference it without checking, crashing the slave.

sizeOfPDO, called during state transitions, uses the subindex-0 count of the SM-assign and PDO-mapping objects as loop bounds without checking those counts against the descriptor array sizes. On builds where those subindex-0 values are writable via SDO, a master can write 0xFF and cause sizeOfPDO to read past the end of the descriptor arrays on the next transition to SAFEOP.

The FoE DATA frame handler computes the payload length from the master-supplied mailbox length field and passes it directly to FOE_fwrite. The length is checked against the remaining file capacity but not against the physical mailbox buffer size. A master can declare a large length while sending a short frame, causing FOE_fwrite to read past the end of the mailbox buffer.

EOE_set_ip reads each network parameter field (MAC, IP, subnet, gateway, DNS IP, DNS name) from the mailbox payload before checking whether the payload is large enough to contain them. The single bounds check at the end of the function does not prevent the reads from happening. A master can send a Set-IP frame with all flags set and mbxheader.length equal to the minimum, causing all reads to access memory past the end of the payload.

The CoE entry gate accepts frames with mbxheader.length as low as COE_MINIMUM_LENGTH (8), but a normal SDO Download requires at least COE_HEADERSIZE (10) bytes of CoE payload to carry its header fields. With mbxheader.length of 8 or 9, the segmented-transfer branch misevaluates due to unsigned wrap, leaving the declared SDO size unclamped. copy2mbx then reads that many bytes starting past the end of the actual payload and writes them into the object buffer.

FOE_read and FOE_write store the filename length as uint8_t, truncating it modulo 256. When (mbxheader.length - ESC_FOEHSIZE) is a multiple of 256, the length becomes 0. Additionally, a request whose mailbox length equals ESC_FOEHSIZE exactly also produces a length of 0 without any truncation. In both cases FOE_fopen calls strncmp with a length of 0, which always returns equal, so the first registered file whose password is 0 is opened regardless of the filename the master sent.

An object dictionary entry can carry write-access flags and still have a NULL data pointer, for example when a constant value is held in the value field rather than in addressable storage. The CoE SDO download handler checked write access but not whether storage was present, then wrote the master-supplied payload through the NULL pointer.

The CoE SDO upload handler enters its normal-response path (used for objects longer than 4 bytes) and passes (objd + nsub)->data directly to the pre-object handler and to the response copy. Entries that hold a constant in the value field have data set to NULL; a master can request such an entry and cause a NULL pointer dereference in the upload path.

The FoE file table allows entries to omit a write handler by setting write_function to NULL, making the file read-only. FOE_fopen did not check whether write_function was present before accepting a write request; a master sending a WRQ for a read-only file caused a call through a NULL function pointer.

The EoE receive and transmit paths call the handle_recv_buffer and fetch_send_buffer callbacks without first checking whether they are set. Both callbacks are documented as optional; an application that omits either one causes a call through a NULL function pointer when the first EoE frame arrives or when the transmit polling loop runs.

ESC_foeprocess can be reached by an incoming mailbox frame before the application calls FOE_config to supply the file table and flush buffer pointers. When foe_cfg or its fbuffer field is NULL the handler dereferenced those pointers while processing the frame, causing a NULL pointer dereference.

ESC_eoeprocess and ESC_eoeprocess_tx can be reached before the application calls EOE_config to supply the callback table pointer. When eoe_cfg is NULL the receive handler dereferenced it while processing an incoming EoE frame, and the transmit polling function dereferenced it on each cycle, causing NULL pointer dereferences.

The PDO mapping bit lengths stored in the mapping objects are writable by the master via SDO. sizeOfPDO summed them without checking the total against the size of the rxpdo[] or txpdo[] process data buffers. A master can craft a mapping whose total bit count exceeds those buffers, causing COE_pdoPack and COE_pdoUnpack to write past their ends during each process data cycle after the PREOP to SAFEOP transition.

An object dictionary entry that holds a constant has no process data storage and carries a NULL data pointer. sizeOfPDO did not check for this when resolving a mapped entry to its descriptor. A master that maps such an entry to a PDO causes COE_pdoPack or COE_pdoUnpack to dereference the NULL data pointer on every process data exchange after the mapping is activated.

The CoE complete-access download handler iterated over all subindices of an object and wrote the master-supplied payload into each writable entry. Entries that hold a constant have write-access flags set but carry a NULL data pointer. The handler did not check for this and wrote the master payload through the NULL pointer.

The SDO Information Get Object Description and Get Entry Description responses copy the object or entry name into the mailbox data area and then write a null terminator byte. The copy loops ran up to the last available byte in the buffer, leaving no room for the terminator. When an object or entry name exactly fills the available space the terminator is written one byte past the end of the mailbox data buffer.

@fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.0 through 4.0.9, when Fastify routing is configured to be case-insensitive, the router folds the request path to lower case in a way that maps certain non-ASCII Unicode characters to ASCII letters, but @fastify/express matches Express mount paths against the decoded path without applying the same folding. The two disagree, so a request that spells a letter of a mount path with an equivalent Unicode character is routed to the protected handler while the path-scoped middleware mounted on that path never matches and is skipped. An unauthenticated client can therefore reach a handler that an authentication, authorization, or rate-limiting middleware was meant to protect, though only when the application enables case-insensitive routing and the mount path contains an affected letter. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

The YMC Filter plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Sensitive Information Exposure in all versions up to, and including, 3.14.1 via the 'post_status' parameter. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to extract retrieve rendered grid HTML containing titles, excerpts, author names, dates, categories, tags, and thumbnails of private, draft, pending, and future posts they do not have permission to view. Exposure only occurs when an administrator has configured at least one non-publish status in the filter grid's Appearance → Post Status setting, as attacker-supplied statuses are intersected with this administrator-defined allowlist before being passed to WP_Query.

The Product Import Export for WooCommerce – CSV Product Importer & Exporter plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'author (initial store via wp-comments-post.php) / CSV cell on import' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.6.9 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. The exploit requires an administrator to approve the attacker's review, then export and re-import it using the plugin's default column mapping, with the import taking the INSERT branch — which occurs automatically on any site whose database table prefix is not the literal 'wp_', when the CSV has no comment_ID mapping, or when the original review has been trashed. Successful exploitation additionally requires an action by an administrator — the attacker cannot trigger the vulnerability on their own.
products: webtoffee / Product Import Export for WooCommerce – CSV Product Importer & Exporter

description: The Accept Stripe Payments plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored DOM-Based Cross-Site Scripting via the 'href of any <a> element containing 'asp_action=show_pp&product_id='' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.1.4 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. The Newsletter  WordPress plugin before 9.4.0 does not check that a visitor is really the subscriber before showing them newsletters marked as private, and accepts a weaker subscriber identifier that anyone can obtain by submitting a known subscriber's email address to the public subscription form, allowing unauthenticated attackers who know a subscriber's email address to read every private newsletter sent to that subscriber.

The Newsletter  WordPress plugin before 9.4.0 does not properly validate the destination of the redirect performed when a subscriber changes their list membership from a newsletter link, checking only that it begins with the site's URL, allowing unauthenticated attackers to redirect users to external sites whose address starts with the site's URL.

The Newsletter  WordPress plugin before 9.4.0 does not protect its unsubscription actions against Cross-Site Request Forgery for subscribers it identifies from its own tracking cookie, allowing attackers to unsubscribe a subscriber from the site's newsletter by making them visit a malicious page.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not prevent placeholders in a shortcode attribute from being expanded with unescaped nested shortcode output, allowing users with a role as low as contributor to perform Stored Cross-Site Scripting attacks.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not restrict which PHP functions a shortcode's filter attribute can call, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to remove WordPress' term-slug sanitization and perform SQL injection attacks through another shortcode's taxonomy term attribute.

The Shortcodes Ultimate  WordPress plugin before 7.9.1 does not restrict the content type of its lightbox shortcode, allowing users with the contributor role and above to make the lightbox fetch HTML from an attacker-controlled server and insert it into the page unsanitised, leading to Stored Cross-Site Scripting when a user opens the lightbox.

The FluentCommunity  WordPress plugin before 2.13.0 does not apply the per-link visibility rules of space sidebar links when listing spaces in its space discovery feature, allowing unauthenticated visitors to retrieve the titles and URLs of links restricted to logged-in users or specific memberships, as well as disabled links, for every public and private space.

The FluentCommunity  WordPress plugin before 2.7.0 does not verify that the user is allowed to manage the space it actually modifies or deletes, allowing a user who administers any one space to modify or permanently delete any other space on the site, together with its posts, comments, reactions and memberships.

The FluentCommunity  WordPress plugin before 2.13.0 does not verify that a referenced media item belongs to the user, or is not already attached elsewhere, before re-linking it to their own content, and its media identifiers are predictable from public post data, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to take over and delete media uploaded by other users, including administrators.

The Keywords to Links Converter WordPress plugin before 2.2.5 does not sanitise and escape a parameter before using it in a SQL statement via an AJAX action available to any authenticated user, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to perform SQL injection attacks and read arbitrary data from the database.

The FluentCommunity  WordPress plugin before 2.8.0 does not check that a lesson belongs to the course a course creator is authorised to manage before moving it, allowing a user with the Course Creator role to move lessons out of other creators' courses into their own and read their content.

The Keywords to Links Converter WordPress plugin before 2.2.5 does not validate a value submitted to one of its AJAX actions before saving it as an option that it later uses in an arithmetic operation on every admin and front-end request, allowing users with a role as low as Subscriber to make the whole site return a fatal error until the option is manually reset.

The Titan Anti-spam & Security  WordPress plugin before 7.5.5 does not protect or remove the diagnostic archive it writes to the uploads folder when an administrator exports its logs, and names it after the export date alone, allowing unauthenticated visitors to download the Titan Anti-spam & Security  WordPress plugin before 7.5.5's logs, including visitor IP addresses, and the site's system information.

The RSVPMaker for Toastmasters WordPress plugin before 6.9.3 does not sanitise and escape a parameter before outputting it back in an admin page, leading to a Reflected Cross-Site Scripting which could be used against high privilege users such as admin.

The Newsletter  WordPress plugin before 9.4.0 does not keep a subscriber's secret key out of the redirect it returns after a subscription request when double opt-in is enabled, allowing unauthenticated attackers to confirm a subscription for any email address without access to its mailbox and, when the address already has an unconfirmed subscription, to reset that record with their own details.

@fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions before 4.0.10, the plugin passes Express a request URL that does not always match the path Fastify's router dispatched, so path-scoped Express middleware can be skipped while the route handler still runs. Several request forms trigger the mismatch, including percent-decoding that rewrites a backslash to a slash or double-decodes an encoded percent sign, and a request target that begins with an asterisk, so the middleware and the handler disagree on the path or on parameter and query values. An unauthenticated client can therefore reach a handler that an authentication, authorization, or rate-limiting middleware was meant to protect, with no special configuration required. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

@fastify/middie is the middleware engine for the Fastify web framework. In versions up to and including 9.3.7, middie matches path-scoped middleware against its own reading of the request path, which can differ from the path Fastify's router uses to dispatch the request. When the two disagree, the router can route a request to a handler covered by a middleware mount while middie skips that middleware, so an unauthenticated client reaches a handler that an authentication, authorization, or rate-limiting middleware was meant to protect, with no special configuration required. The mismatch is triggered by empty parameter or wildcard values, request targets that do not begin with a slash, and literal percent characters in a mount path. The issue is fixed in @fastify/middie 9.3.8, and users should upgrade to 9.3.8 or later.

@fastify/swagger-ui is the plugin that serves Swagger UI documentation for Fastify applications. In versions 2.1.0 through 6.1.4, the authentication hooks that applications register to protect the documentation are applied to every route the plugin adds except the bundled static asset instance. When the option that serves bundled UI files from a local directory is enabled, that instance exposes every file in the directory without credentials, so a specification file an operator meant to keep behind the documentation login becomes reachable by an unauthenticated client who knows or guesses its name. Access is read-only and limited to files in that directory. The issue is fixed in @fastify/swagger-ui 6.1.5, which applies the same authentication hooks to the static asset route, and users should upgrade to 6.1.5 or later.

@fastify/rate-limit is the rate-limiting plugin for the Fastify web framework. Starting in version 11.1.0, the plugin documented a manual flow for limiting failed login attempts that peeks at the limiter, runs the password check, and consumes a slot only on failure. Because the peek and the consume are two separate store operations with the password check in between, concurrent requests can all pass the peek before any slot is consumed, so in versions 11.1.0 through 11.2.2 a burst of requests runs far more failed attempts than the configured limit, and the sequential path also allowed one attempt more than configured. The default per-request limiter is not affected. The issue is fixed in @fastify/rate-limit 11.3.0, which makes the manual flow atomic by reserving a slot in a single operation and refunding it only on success, and users should upgrade to 11.3.0 or later.

The BlockStrap Page Builder – Bootstrap Blocks plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'comment' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 0.1.65 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. description: The Coupon Creator plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'post_title' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 3.6.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. The Fastcache by Host.it plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Reflected Cross-Site Scripting via the 's' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 1.7.14 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that execute if they can successfully trick a user into performing an action such as clicking on a link. This code path is only reachable when both the Light Images feature and the DOMDocument entity-decode branch are enabled (lightimgs_status = 1 and img_processing_entity_decode = 1), which reflect the default plugin configuration.

@fastify/express is a compatibility layer that lets Express middleware run inside the Fastify web framework. In versions 4.0.7 through 4.0.9, the plugin does not rewrite regular-expression mount paths to account for a parameterized plugin prefix, so when middleware is mounted with a regular expression inside a plugin registered under a parameterized prefix, the Express matcher treats the prefix parameter as literal text and never matches the real request path. As a result, Express silently skips that middleware while Fastify still runs the route handler, so an application that relies on regular-expression mounted middleware for authentication or authorization inside a parameterized-prefix plugin exposes protected routes to unauthenticated clients. No special configuration is required beyond a parameterized prefix and a regular-expression mount. The issue is fixed in @fastify/express 4.0.10, and users should upgrade to 4.0.10 or later.

A flaw was found in Quay. Insufficient validation of repository notification webhook URLs allows an authenticated administrator to trigger Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). By specifying an internal URL or a redirect to an internal destination, an attacker can force the Quay worker to issue unauthorized HTTP requests to internal network locations and cloud metadata services.

A vulnerability was determined in MaysWind AriaNg-Native up to 1.3.14. Affected by this issue is the function shell.openPath of the file main/ipc/main-process.js of the component IPC Handler. Patch name: ac5a4bcf102f605b160f19fcc9fbaec67f9596d7. You should upgrade the affected component.

A security vulnerability has been detected in Bytebase DBHub up to 2.0.0. Impacted is the function escapeHatchFunctionKeywords of the file src/utils/allowed-keywords.ts of the component Read Only Mode. The manipulation of the argument tool leads to incomplete blacklist. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A vulnerability was detected in eigent-ai eigent up to 1.0.2. Executing a manipulation can lead to out-of-bounds read. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit has been published and may be used. Parse Server 2.5.0 before 8.6.121 and 9.0.0 before 9.11.1-alpha.1 does not handle a failure to serialize an object after a beforeSave trigger, leaving the request unsettled and terminating the server process. A remote attacker able to update an object in a class with a beforeSave trigger can send a dot notation key below a non-object field, such as a timestamp, to crash the server for all clients.

Parse Server before 8.6.122 and 9.0.0 before 9.11.1-alpha.2 does not prevent dot notation keys from changing a field that a beforeSave trigger keeps constant or reverts, affecting Object, Array, GeoPoint, Polygon, Bytes (on MongoDB), and ACL fields on create and update. A client allowed to write the object can modify such a field, such as a constant role list, to bypass Cloud Code authorization checks.

SiYuan 3.8.0 before 3.8.10 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in LAN sync that allows adjacent unauthenticated attackers to obtain device metadata by advertising a counterfeit peer with a replayed discovery tag. The client sends the sync scope ID, device name, OS, app version, and TLS client certificate to /peer-sync/v1/session/open before validating the server proof.

SiYuan 3.8.0 before 3.8.10 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the serveAssets route that allows unauthenticated attackers to read password-protected document assets via name collisions. Attackers can request GET /assets/<name> when a visible document references the same relative asset name, retrieving the protected file's contents on public-publish instances with Basic Auth disabled.

SiYuan 3.6.0 before 3.6.2 and 3.7.3 before 3.8.10 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the /api/block/getDOMText endpoint, which renders caller-supplied DOM without checking publish access for referenced image paths. When publish authentication is disabled, anonymous visitors can submit DOM referencing a known unpublished, non-encrypted asset path to retrieve its already-cached OCR text.

SiYuan 3.8.0 before 3.8.10 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows anonymous attackers to read indexed asset text referenced only by publish-disabled attribute-view rows. Attackers can request /api/asset/getDocAssets on a public host document to obtain the leaked asset path, then query /api/search/getAssetContentByPath to retrieve the confidential file's full indexed text.

SiYuan 3.6.0 before 3.8.10 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated Readers to read protected documents through block-reference footnote resolution in Markdown export. Attackers can request copyStdMarkdown for a public document referencing a hidden, disabled, or password-protected document to disclose its body text without the publish password.

SiYuan before 3.8.10 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to gain Administrator role by spoofing X-Forwarded-For through a loopback-trusted reverse proxy. Attackers can send requests with Host set to localhost and X-Forwarded-For set to 127.0.0.1 to read private note-history contents via the /history/*path route when no lock-screen password is set.

Grav Form plugin 1.1.0 before 9.1.40 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in Form::uploadFiles(), which sanitizes SVG only when a file's last extension is .svg and accepts markup under unrecognized extensions. Anonymous attackers can upload files like drawing.svg.foo through public any-type upload forms, running script in an administrator's session when opened, enabling super-admin creation on Grav 2.x with Admin2.

Grav API plugin from 1.0.16 before 1.1.11 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows scoped API key holders to override page permission rules because checks read the owning account's authority instead of the key's scopes. Attackers can use keys minted on super-admin accounts to edit, delete or read pages that deny those actions, or use media-scoped keys to change media on read-only pages.

Grav API plugin from 1.0.0 before 1.1.4 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows publishers with media and page write rights to write theme template files through the blueprint-upload endpoint. Attackers can upload a file into a theme's Twig templates folder and include it from sandboxed page Twig to execute commands as the web-server user.

Admidio from 5.0.0 before 5.0.18 contains a path traversal vulnerability in DocumentsService::renameFile() that allows authenticated users to move files outside adm_my_files by supplying an unvalidated adm_new_name value. Attackers with folder upload permission can submit ../ sequences to file_rename_save to write files and create directories in arbitrary writable locations, including the web root.

Admidio from 5.0.17 before 5.0.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject JavaScript by saving a crafted value in their STREET profile field. Attackers can break out of the unencoded title attribute in members_assignment_data.php with an onmouseover handler that executes in the session of role managers hovering over the address icon.

Admidio from 5.0.17 before 5.0.18 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated regular users to upload images into the announcements module by abusing the CKEditor upload handler. Attackers can send id=ann_description to ckeditor_upload_handler.php to store images under adm_my_files/announcements/images and retrieve them via show_image.php, abusing the application as an image host.

Admidio before 5.0.18 contains an insufficient session expiration vulnerability that allows attackers to keep account access after a forgot-password reset because User::setPassword() deletes sessions using the visitor ID instead of the reset user's usr_id. Attackers already holding a victim's session or remember-me cookie can continue using it after the victim resets the password, keeping authenticated access to the account.

Admidio 5.0.0 before 5.0.18 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the Documents & Files renameFile() action that allows authenticated users with folder upload rights to move files outside adm_my_files by supplying ../ sequences in adm_new_name. Attackers can relocate an uploaded SVG containing script to the web root, where it is served inline and executes stored cross-site scripting against administrators for account takeover.

Admidio from 5.0.16 before 5.0.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows users with folder upload rights to store JavaScript by uploading SVG files served inline. Attackers can upload a script-bearing SVG that downloadFile() serves as image/svg+xml inline without nosniff or CSP, executing on the Admidio origin for viewers including unauthenticated visitors.

Admidio 5.0.0 before 5.0.18 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in modules/profile/profile_new.php that allows authenticated Group Leaders to bypass field-level profile restrictions. Attackers can request mode=html_selection to read restricted field values and submit mode=save requests to modify restricted member profile fields.

Admidio before 5.0.18 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in mylist.php that loads list configurations by the list_uuid parameter while checking only the organization, not the owner or private flag. Authenticated users with Lists module access who know a victim's list UUID can read its name, selected profile fields, sort order and filter conditions.

Admidio 5.0.0 before 5.0.18 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows role administrators to inject JavaScript by placing quote-breaking payloads in role names rendered unencoded in the data-message attribute in modules/profile/roles_functions.php. Attackers can execute scripts when a full administrator views an affected profile page, stealing the CSRF token to assign themselves the Administrator role.

Admidio from 5.0.2 before 5.0.17 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability that allows any logged-in member to read server files by placing local paths in img src attributes of eCard messages. Attackers can send an eCard to their own account so sendEcard() embeds files like adm_my_files/config.php via addEmbeddedImage(), disclosing database credentials and /etc/passwd.

Vikunja from 2.4.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the richtext converter that allows authenticated project writers to exhaust server memory and CPU by storing tables with unbounded rowspan and colspan values. Any project reader or CalDAV client can trigger the expansion through markdown task reads, CalDAV GETs, or the frontend editor, producing 100 MB responses from a 64-byte description.

Vikunja from 0.19.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated users to exhaust CPU by supplying unbounded business-day operands in datemath filters. Attackers can send task or time-tracking filters like due_date > now+999999999999b, triggering a per-day loop in go-datemath that pins CPU cores and exhausts the server.

Vikunja from 0.21.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated users to exhaust memory and CPU by creating tasks with many reminders and long titles. Attackers can store a task whose ParseAlarms rendering in pkg/caldav/caldav.go uses quadratic string concatenation, causing every CalDAV read, including other members' automatic syncs, to allocate gigabytes.

Vikunja from 0.21.0 before 2.8.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows authenticated users to trigger instance-wide database writes by setting a project position below 0.1. Attackers can repeatedly send PUT requests to /api/v2/projects/{id} so recalculateProjectPositions updates every user's root projects, holding SQLite's write lock and degrading availability.

Vikunja from 0.18.0 before 2.8.0 contains a resource amplification vulnerability in pkg/models/export.go that allows authenticated users to exhaust server memory by exporting heavily related tasks. Attackers can relate many tasks to one task with a large description and request a user export, causing an out-of-memory crash for all users.

Vikunja from 0.19.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated CalDAV users to exhaust server CPU by uploading VTODO properties with many parameters. Attackers can PUT an iCalendar body with thousands of parameters on one line to any valid project ID, triggering superlinear parsing before permission checks.

Vikunja from 1.0.0 before 2.8.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability that allows authenticated users to crash the server by uploading extreme-width images as task attachments. Attackers can request the attachment preview endpoint so Lanczos resampling allocates width-proportional weight tables, OOM-killing the process repeatedly with sub-megabyte PNGs.

Vikunja from 0.9.0 before 2.8.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows project admins to view share creators' email addresses via the link share list endpoint. Attackers with admin permission can request the project shares endpoint and read the shared_by email field, exposing addresses of creators including former project members.

Vikunja from 2.6.0 before 2.8.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in the Planka migration converter that multiplies task allocations for duplicate list IDs. Attackers controlling a Planka server can return boards with duplicate list IDs and many cards to exhaust memory and OOM-kill the Vikunja process.

Vikunja from 0.8.0 before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows authenticated project readers to amplify response size by repeating requested properties in CalDAV PROPFIND requests. Attackers can send PROPFIND requests to the dav projects endpoint with hundreds of duplicate calendar-data properties to exhaust server memory, CPU, and bandwidth.

Vikunja from 2.2.1 before 2.8.0 contains a TOTP replay protection bypass in ValidateTOTPPasscode that allows attackers to reuse consumed codes by padding them with whitespace. Attackers with valid credentials who observe a used passcode can resubmit it whitespace-padded to the login API within the validity window to obtain a session token.

Vikunja from 0.16.0 before 2.8.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that writes users' Trello API tokens to application logs and Sentry by formatting provider errors verbatim in listeners.go. When a Trello migration fails with a transport error, the URL error embeds the token query parameter, letting anyone with log or telemetry access obtain the reusable third-party credential.

Vikunja 2.3.0 before 2.8.0 contains an uncontrolled memory allocation in the CSV migration module because it does not de-duplicate label column mappings or cap labels per row, and enforces the item limit only after the full import is built. Authenticated users can send one request to /api/v2/migration/csv/migrate with repeated label mappings or many labels per row, exhausting memory until the server is OOM-killed.

Vikunja from 0.20.5 before 2.8.0 contains a login cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the OpenID Connect callback in OpenIdAuth.vue that accepts a valueless state parameter. Attackers can send a crafted callback link with an empty state and their own authorization code to silently log victims into the attacker's account and view the victims' entered data.

Vikunja 0.17.0 before 2.8.0 builds the task.deleted notification and webhook payload, including related tasks, with the deleting user's permissions and sends it to all project subscribers without per-recipient authorization checks. A user subscribed to a project, or owning its webhook, receives full data of related tasks in private projects they cannot read when a task in their project is deleted.

Vikunja from 2.2.0 before 2.8.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read other users' private projects through the tasks.overdue webhook payload. Attackers can register a personal tasks.overdue webhook with one subscribed overdue task, then receive project titles, descriptions, and owner IDs from other users' reminders at external URLs.

Vikunja from 0.14.0 before 2.8.0 contains a mass assignment vulnerability that allows authenticated users to set json-hidden fields by sending XML request bodies to the v1 API. Attackers can set BackgroundFileID on project creation to download any stored file via the background endpoint, or create bots with IsAdmin set to gain instance-admin access.

Vikunja from 1.0.0 before 2.8.0 contains an account takeover vulnerability that allows attackers to hijack SSO identities by planting local accounts with unverified victim emails. When emailfallback is enabled, attackers register or edit a local account using the victim's email, causing the victim's first OIDC login to link into the attacker-controlled account and expose their data.

OpenRemote from 1.2.0 before 1.34.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in AlarmFacade that allows restricted users with write:rules to create alarms for assets outside their ruleset subtree. Attackers can deploy a JSON asset-scoped ruleset using target.custom asset ids to create HIGH severity alarms and trigger operator notifications about arbitrary in-realm assets.

OpenRemote core before 1.34.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in UserAssetProvisioningMQTTHandler that allows unauthenticated attackers to impersonate provisioned devices without proof of private key possession. Attackers can publish a known device's public certificate to the provisioning request topic, authenticating their anonymous MQTT connection as the device's service account to read and modify assets.

SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows clients with table write access to persist writes refused by THROWing table events within interactive transactions. Attackers can run a guarded statement via RPC begin and query, ignore the returned error, and commit to persist the record and event side effects.

SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 prints SURREAL_PASS and SURREAL_TOKEN environment variable values in clear text in the --help and -h output of CLI commands such as surreal start, sql, import, export, and mcp, because the arguments do not set clap's hide_env_values. Anyone who later sees that terminal output, for example in shell logs, CI logs, or screen shares, can obtain root database credentials.

SurrealDB 2.2.0 before 4.0.0 includes the record id of a referencing row in the error returned when a delete is blocked by an ON DELETE REJECT reference, without checking the caller's SELECT permission on that row. An authenticated principal with DELETE permission can attempt to delete a referenced record and read the rejection error to learn the existence and exact ids of referencing records hidden by row-level SELECT permissions.

SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in its filesystem storage bucket that only canonicalizes the bucket root, not descendant symlinks. Attackers can reference paths through a pre-existing symlink inside the bucket that pass the lexical prefix check, reading and writing files across the host filesystem.

SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a capability check bypass in its embedded JavaScript scripting engine, where the surrealdb.functions bridge calls the internal fnc::synchronous() and fnc::asynchronous() dispatchers without enforcing function capability checks. Authenticated users denied access to built-in functions in SurrealQL can execute them by calling them through surrealdb.functions from embedded JavaScript.

SurrealDB 3.1.0 before 4.0.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in its Model Context Protocol (MCP) server because the identifier validator (consume_backtick_ident and validate_identifier) treats the first backtick as the closing delimiter, ignoring escape characters that the SurrealQL parser honors. Attackers can supply MCP tool arguments containing an escaped backtick to break out of the quoted identifier and execute arbitrary SurrealQL statements.

SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in its bucket storage layer on Windows, where ObjectKey::check_no_traversal splits object keys only on forward slashes while FileStore::to_os_path treats backslashes as directory separators. Attackers can supply object keys such as /..\bucket2\secret to bypass the traversal check and read or modify files in other buckets.

SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability in direct filesystem buckets because BucketController::check_permission evaluates key-based ACLs against the un-normalized object key, while FileStore::to_os_path collapses '..' sequences without a traversal check. An authenticated tenant permitted only for certain keys can supply a key such as /public/../private/confidential.txt to read, write, or delete arbitrary files within the storage root.

SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass that allows users with the read-only VIEWER role to modify database schema, because CREATE on a nonexistent table implicitly defines it without the DEFINE TABLE permission check applied to explicit definitions. Authenticated VIEWER users can issue CREATE statements in non-STRICT databases to add arbitrary empty SCHEMALESS tables, cluttering schemas or colliding with application table names.

SurrealDB 3.0.4 before 4.0.0 does not apply operator-configured WebSocket frame, message, and buffer size limits to the GraphQL WebSocket upgrade handler at GET /graphql, falling back to permissive library defaults. Unauthenticated remote attackers who supply the target namespace and database in request headers can hold up to 64 MiB of in-flight data per concurrent connection, exhausting server memory and degrading availability.

SurrealDB from 2.2.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in Document::purge_references that lets authenticated users bypass target table PERMISSIONS by triggering REFERENCE ON DELETE cascades. Attackers can delete a referenced record to delete, unset, or run CUSTOM expressions on referencing records despite PERMISSIONS FOR delete or update NONE.

SurrealDB before 4.0.0 contains a guard bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to execute write subqueries by embedding them in LIVE query WHERE clauses or field projections. Attackers can inject CREATE, UPDATE, DELETE, or RELATE statements that run atomically inside other users' triggering transactions, amplifying writes and exfiltrating document data after permission revocation.

SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows any user able to run queries to crash the server by triggering unchecked decimal overflow in math::sum or math::product. Attackers can submit a query summing or multiplying large decimal literals or aggregate stored decimals with GROUP ALL, causing a rust_decimal panic that terminates the entire server process.

SurrealKV before 1.1.0 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in the safe InternalKeyRef::from_encoded constructor, which only checks key length with a debug-only assertion. Callers passing keys shorter than 16 bytes, or crafted or corrupted SSTable blocks, trigger unchecked length underflow in timestamp(), seq_num() and trailer(), reading heap bytes before the allocation or panicking.

SurrealDB before 4.0.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in filter_fields_by_permission that allows authenticated record users to read denied child field values. Attackers can query rows where overlapping items[*] and items[*].secret permissions compact arrays, causing shifted elements to retain field values denied by SELECT permissions.

SurrealDB 3.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains a permission bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated low-privilege database users to read restricted records by calling the GET /export endpoint. Attackers can export raw records that skip table SELECT predicates and field-level SELECT permissions, exposing other users' rows and hidden fields.

SurrealDB 1.0.0 before 4.0.0 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to shadow protected $access, $auth, and $token variables by binding them as FOR loop variables. Attackers can wrap queries in nested FOR loops with forged values to satisfy table permission predicates, enabling unauthorized reads, modifications, or deletions as a VIEWER.

SurrealDB from 3.2.0 before 3.3.4 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows record users to update protected rows by exploiting table-level PERMISSIONS FOR update predicates referencing COMPUTED fields. Because check_update_permissions evaluates the predicate before computed fields are populated, the field reads as NONE and deny-intended predicates like blocked != true pass, letting attackers modify records.

better-auth 1.3.0 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the admin plugin's /admin/update-user endpoint that lets roles holding user:update change another user's phoneNumber and phoneNumberVerified fields. Attackers can set their own verified phone number on a higher-privileged account and sign in via phone OTP to take it over.

Better Auth 0.4.9 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains an OAuth sign-in authentication flaw that treats unverified provider emails as verified, including string "false" email_verified claims, unchecked generic OAuth profile/ID-token subject mismatches, and ignored Zoom provider options. Attackers holding a victim's address unverified at an affected provider can sign in, link to the victim's local account, and obtain its session.

Better Auth (better-auth, @better-auth/kysely-adapter, and @better-auth/drizzle-adapter) before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains a race condition with MySQL or MariaDB serial IDs because the inserted row's ID is read via a separate LAST_INSERT_ID() query that may run on a different pooled connection. Under concurrent load, a user signing in can receive another user's session and act as that user.

better-auth 1.3.7 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains a race condition in the emailOTP plugin attempt counter, collision-prone email change code keys, and accent-insensitive email lookups. Unauthenticated attackers can send concurrent guesses exceeding allowedAttempts to brute-force OTPs and sign in or reset passwords, signed-in users can verify addresses they do not own, and attackers receiving mail at accent-variant addresses can reset victims' passwords.

better-auth 1.4.0 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains an improper authentication vulnerability because email-change links record the old and new addresses but not the requesting user. Attackers can open a still-valid link issued for their own account after a victim registers the attacker's released old address, gaining a session and changing the victim's email to one they control.

@better-auth/electron 1.5.0-beta.12 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 accepts any validly signed value as its transfer cookie and returns the full endpoint context, including the auth secret and social provider client secrets, in sign-in responses. Authenticated users can obtain these secrets to forge sessions as other users. Attackers knowing a password can exchange desktop authorization codes issued before two-factor verification to bypass the second factor.

@better-auth/stripe 1.2.0-beta.18 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability because the stripeCustomerId user field accepts values from sign-up and update-user requests, letting a user replace their own Stripe customer ID with another customer's. Attackers who know another customer's Stripe ID can open that customer's billing portal to view invoices and billing details, change payment methods, and cancel or modify subscriptions.

better-auth 1.5.5 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability in the organization plugin, where the creator role check compares the raw invitation role string while later checks trim it. Admins or other non-creator roles that can invite can submit a padded role such as " owner" that becomes owner on acceptance, allowing deletion of the organization and removal of original owners.

@better-auth/passkey 1.4.0-beta.16 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5, and the passkey plugin in better-auth 1.2.0-beta.18 before 1.4.0, do not confirm WebAuthn user verification when userVerification is "required" and take the expected origin from the request instead of configuration. Users can register or use passkeys without the required PIN or biometric check, and passkey responses created on another origin under the same relying party ID may be accepted.

better-auth from 0.8.1-beta.5 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5, and @better-auth/passkey from 1.6.25 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5, let revoked sessions stay valid because secondary storage session lists are updated non-atomically and some routes trust cookie-cached sessions. An attacker holding a valid session can evade bulk revocation or bans, or use a revoked cached session to register a passkey or create a lasting session.

better-auth 0.4.12-beta.7 before 1.7.16 and 1.8.0-beta.0 before 1.8.0-beta.5 contains an improper authentication vulnerability in the phone number plugin that lets sign-up and other flows save unverified phone numbers, which phone OTP sign-in then uses to select the account. Attackers can attach a victim's number to an attacker-controlled account so the victim's valid OTP sign-in yields a session for that account, exposing data the victim then enters.

ArcadeDB 26.3.1 before 26.11.1 contains a read-only bypass vulnerability that allows server administrators to commit writes through the MCP read-only query tool by submitting Groovy-fallback Gremlin scripts. GremlinQueryEngine.analyze() evaluates scripts like Graph API addVertex calls on the auto or groovy engine and classifies them as READ, persisting writes the read-only restriction should refuse.

ArcadeDB before 26.11.1 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the Redis protocol handler, which neither replies to nor closes a pre-authentication connection when it receives an array whose first element is not a string. Unauthenticated attackers can resend such an array just within the 30-second socket idle timeout to hold connections open indefinitely and exhaust RedisNetworkExecutor threads.

ArcadeDB before 26.11.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read schema definitions of denied types through listings ignoring per-type ACLs. Attackers can query the PostgreSQL wire catalog, GraphQL introspection, or MCP get_schema to reveal property names, indexes, inheritance, and materialized view SQL.

ArcadeDB 26.2.1 before 26.11.1 contains an observable response discrepancy in MCPToolUtils.resolveDatabase, which checks database existence before authorization and returns distinct 'not authorized' and 'does not exist' errors; separately, a failed Bolt LOGON from READY leaves the previous principal bound after RESET. Authenticated MCP callers can enumerate names of databases they are not granted by probing tools such as query or get_schema.

ArcadeDB from 26.7.1 before 26.11.1 contains an information disclosure vulnerability because LSMTreeFullTextIndex computes BM25 corpus statistics over all buckets of the indexed type, ignoring bucket access control on subtypes. Authenticated users with read access to a supertype but not its subtype can run EXPLAIN or PROFILE on full-text queries and read totalDocs and per-term df values to count hidden subtype documents containing chosen terms.

ArcadeDB 21.10.1 before 26.11.1 contains a resource-limit bypass vulnerability that allows restricted users to evade per-group readTimeout because limits are applied to shared cached statements and plans. Attackers can run SQL text previously cached by an unrestricted principal to skip timeouts, or impose their own timeout and limit on root and other users.

ArcadeDB native-image server builds 26.8.1 before 26.11.1 contain an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated clients to perform writes through read-only query paths by nesting statements in SELECT. Missing reflection metadata leaves SqlAstInspector with an empty AST, letting INSERT in projections or LET clauses persist via the query endpoint, MCP read-only mode, and HA follower routing.

ArcadeDB 25.8.1 before 26.11.1 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability because per-type ACLs are keyed by type name, renames are not propagated to the permission configuration, and requestAccessOnType allows unknown type names by default. Authenticated users holding only updateSchema can run ALTER TYPE NAME on a denied type to gain read, DELETE and TRUNCATE access, immediately for TIMESERIES types and after the next security rebuild for record-backed types.

ArcadeDB from 26.11.1-SNAPSHOT before 26.11.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to skip per-type ACL checks when a database is opened on demand. Attackers can send the first POST /api/v1/batch/{database} request to a closed database to read and write types they are not entitled to access.

actix-http 3.0.0 before 3.20.3 contains a denial of service vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to exhaust memory by sending large-window brotli request bodies. Attackers can send an 850-byte body with Content-Encoding: br declaring a 2^30 window, forcing about 1 GiB of decoder allocation per request and OOM-killing servers.

actix-http 3.18.10 before 3.20.2 contains an HTTP request smuggling vulnerability in its chunked decoder, which treats a bare LF after the last chunk as the start of a trailer section. Attackers can send a body ending in 0\r\n\n through a connection-reusing proxy so the next request's body is parsed as new requests, bypassing WAF or upstream protections.

actix-files before 0.7.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows remote unauthenticated attackers to read hidden files by requesting Windows 8.3 short-name aliases. Attackers can request short names like ENV~1 or GIT~1/config to bypass the leading-dot check in actix_files::Files and retrieve .env secrets and .git contents.

Rclone from 1.56.0 before 1.76.0 contains a timing side-channel vulnerability in its htpasswd authentication middleware that allows unauthenticated attackers to enumerate valid usernames. Attackers can send HTTP Basic Auth requests with wrong passwords and measure response times, because bcrypt verification runs only for existing users, enabling targeted password guessing.

Rclone from 1.46.0 before 1.76.0 contains a memory exhaustion vulnerability in the remote control server that allows unauthenticated clients to crash rclone by sending oversized JSON bodies. Attackers can POST large JSON payloads to protected RC methods, which handlePost decodes before authorization checks, triggering out-of-memory termination and interrupting transfers.

rclone 1.67.0 before 1.76.0 contains a credential leak vulnerability in the Ulozto backend that sends X-Auth-Token and X-User-Token headers to unintended hosts on HTTP redirect because downloads use the authenticated f.rest client instead of f.cdn. Attackers who can observe or redirect CDN download traffic can capture the long-lived API key and session token to gain persistent access to the victim's Ulozto storage.

Rclone 1.49.0 before 1.76.0 contains an improper authentication vulnerability in Proxy.Call that lets revoked users keep access because cached auth-proxy answers are never revalidated. Revoked users of serve sftp, ftp, http, or webdav can reconnect within five minutes using their original credentials to retain access indefinitely.

Rclone from 1.51.0 before 1.76.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in serve sftp --auth-proxy because the generateCacheKey cache key omits the authentication method. Attackers knowing a victim's base64 public key can submit it as a password from the same client IP to reuse the cached entry and gain read-write VFS access.

rclone before 1.76.0 leaks credentials in its swift, netstorage and seafile backends, which follow HTTP redirects using Go's default policy: swift and netstorage send auth headers or passwords on cross-host or HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects, and seafile sends API tokens or passwords on same-host HTTPS-to-HTTP redirects. Attackers receiving or observing a redirect issued by the configured endpoint can capture these credentials to access storage or replay signed requests.

rclone from 1.59.0 before 1.76.0 contains a confinement escape in the local backend's setXattr function that lets attackers write user.* extended attributes outside the destination root via a planted symlink. Attackers who plant a symlink to an outside directory with a pre-existing child can use --links --metadata operations to set attacker-chosen user.* xattrs on files outside the destination.

AzuraCast before 0.24.1 contains an improper authorization vulnerability in the /api/station/{station_id}/profile/edit endpoint that exposes and accepts Icecast/Shoutcast passwords for users holding Manage Station Profile without Manage Station Broadcasting. Authenticated station users can read the admin, source, relay and streamer passwords via GET to administer Icecast or broadcast to listeners, or overwrite them via PUT to lock out operators.

AzuraCast 0.19.0 before 0.24.1 contains an improper authorization vulnerability that allows users with station media rights to add tracks to other stations' playlists by supplying foreign playlist ids to the single-file edit endpoint. Attackers can send sequential playlist ids in the playlists array to inject entries into other stations' AutoDJ rotations and public now-playing metadata, causing failed playback slots.

AzuraCast before 0.24.1 fails to escape backslashes in Liquidsoap annotation values, allowing media managers to break out of quoted annotation strings. Attackers can set a crafted ID3 title ending in a backslash to inject a process: protocol URI, achieving OS command execution in the Liquidsoap container during playback.

Heym before 0.0.148 passes Playwright navigate-step URLs to page.goto() without validating the scheme and runs step-based scripts inside the backend container. A signed-in user who can run workflows can navigate to file:// URLs and use getText to read known-path files such as the Kubernetes ServiceAccount token or Docker secrets.

Coder 2.6.0 before 2.29.21, 2.30.0 before 2.34.10, 2.35.0 before 2.35.8, 2.36.0 before 2.36.5, and 2.37.0 before 2.37.1 contains a denial of service vulnerability in the workspace agent dRPC API, whose handlers dereference unset request sub-messages and unconfigured Tailnet providers without recovering from panics. Attackers holding a workspace agent token can send UpdateLifecycle, UpdateStartup, or BatchUpdateMetadata messages lacking sub-messages, or call RefreshResumeToken or WorkspaceUpdates, to repeatedly crash coderd.

Coder 2.6.0 before 2.29.26, 2.30.0 before 2.34.18, 2.35.0 before 2.37.10, and 2.38.0 before 2.38.6 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability because CSRF exemption patterns in coderd/httpmw/csrf.go are matched as unanchored regular expressions, letting affected API routes skip CSRF token and same-origin checks. Attackers controlling a page same-site with the deployment can make signed-in users' browsers send forged POST requests that recreate dev containers or add users whose names contain derp to organizations.

Coder 2.32.0 before 2.34.17, 2.35.0 before 2.36.12, 2.37.0 before 2.37.9, and 2.38.0 before 2.38.5 contain a symlink-following flaw in the Coder Agents read_skill_file tool, which validates skill file paths lexically but follows symlinks outside the skill directory. Attackers who place a malicious skill containing a symlinked supporting file in a victim's workspace can leak other workspace files into the model context and chat history when the victim runs a chat using that skill.

pypdf 3.7.1 before 7.0.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows attackers to guess placeholders in encrypted templated documents by analyzing file identifiers. Attackers with a document sharing the same template and access to other documents' file identifiers can recover placeholder contents from encrypted PDFs.

pypdf before 7.0.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability that allows attackers to cause large memory usage by supplying crafted PDF cross-reference streams. Attackers can craft a PDF whose cross-reference stream offsets all point to one large object, exhausting memory in applications parsing the file.

pypdf 2.4.2 before 7.0.0 contains a resource exhaustion vulnerability in its handling of XFA forms that allows attackers to cause excessive memory consumption. Attackers can supply a crafted PDF containing XFA forms with many small fields so that loading the forms consumes large amounts of memory, causing a denial of service.

Frappe Framework before 15.120.1 and 16.x before 16.33.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in file attachment handling that permits arbitrary file read. Authenticated attackers holding a single ordinary role without write permissions can abuse attachment handling to read server files outside the application boundary.

Frappe 8.8.0 before 16.30.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the SMS Settings get_contact_number API that lets attackers read any Contact's phone numbers without permission checks. Attackers can call the endpoint, which uses an uncorrelated EXISTS subquery, to retrieve mobile_no and phone values of arbitrary Contact records, exposing PII.

Frappe ERPNext 4.3.0 before 15.121.6 and 16.x before 16.37.0 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in an endpoint of the Selling and Buying modules, where a request value validated early can be overridden by caller-supplied data that reaches a database query unvalidated. Any authenticated user, including a portal user with no roles, can send crafted requests to extract sensitive data, including active session data, and take over other accounts such as administrators.

Frappe ERPNext 14.0.0 before 15.121.0 and 16.x before 16.34.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Utilities module endpoint that lets any authenticated user retry failed bulk transactions without a role check. Attackers, including portal users with no roles, can send crafted requests for a chosen date to mark site-wide failed bulk transactions as retried, removing them from the normal recovery path, and add background job load.

Frappe ERPNext 15.0.0 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in Assets module endpoints that return a depreciation schedule for a caller-supplied asset without checking read permission on that asset. Authenticated users can name another company's asset to disclose its purchase value, value after depreciation, and depreciation entries.

Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that returns Payment Entries for a readable bank record without checking read permission on each Payment Entry. Authenticated users with an Accounts role can request a readable record to obtain metadata of Payment Entries excluded by their user permissions, such as Cost Center restrictions.

Frappe ERPNext 11.0.0-beta before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.34.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in an Accounts module endpoint that returns the subscription plans linked to a caller-named invoice without checking read permission on that invoice. Authenticated attackers can send crafted requests naming invoices outside their permitted scope to learn whether they belong to subscriptions and read the billed plans.

Frappe ERPNext 7.1.0 before 15.121.0 and 16.x before 16.34.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in Projects module endpoints that return Timesheet data without restricting results to records the caller may read. Any authenticated user, including one with no assigned roles, can send crafted requests to read organisation-wide Timesheet work and billing details.

Frappe ERPNext 12.7.0 before 15.124.0 and 16.x before 16.52.0 stores imported Italian supplier e-invoices as public files in the Regional module, which the server returns without authentication. Unauthenticated attackers can request predictable file URLs built from the supplier's VAT number and invoice sequence to read supplier names, VAT numbers, bank account details and line items.

Frappe ERPNext 8.2.5 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in Manufacturing module endpoints that check only document-type write access, not permission on each Work Order. Authenticated users restricted by User Permissions can send crafted requests naming another company's Work Order to stop, resume or close it.

Frappe ERPNext 5.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in the Buying module: the endpoint that closes and reopens Purchase Orders checks only document-type write permission, not per-document User Permissions. Authenticated users with Purchase Order write access can send crafted requests naming another company's Purchase Order to change its status.

Frappe ERPNext 5.0.0 before 15.121.4 and 16.x before 16.36.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability in a Selling module endpoint that checks only document-type write permission, not permission on each Sales Order, when closing or reopening Sales Orders. Authenticated users restricted by User Permissions can send crafted requests naming another company's Sales Order to close or reopen it outside their restriction.

Frappe ERPNext 14.47.0 before 15.122.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the Accounts module where a method on accounting vouchers creates and submits Repost Accounting Ledger documents with permission checks skipped. Authenticated users with read access to a Sales Invoice, Purchase Invoice, Payment Entry, Journal Entry, or Purchase Receipt can call it to delete and repost that voucher's General Ledger entries, an action restricted to System Managers.

Frappe ERPNext 13.0.0 before 15.124.2 and 16.x before 16.53.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in a Stock module endpoint that returns item cost data without checking the caller's permissions on the item, company, or warehouse.
